subject: english
text: In 'The Summit Within', which three qualities did Major H.P.S. Ahluwalia say were essential to climb a summit?
explanation: Major H.P.S. Ahluwalia states that endurance, persistence, and willpower are the three qualities needed to scale any peak.

options.text: Endurance, persistence, and willpower
Strength, speed, and agility
Courage, wealth, and luck
Intelligence, training, and equipment

subject: english
text: Why does the author feel that climbing Everest is not just a physical achievement?
explanation: The author explains that the climber feels a sense of fulfillment, gratitude, and a spiritual awakening that goes far beyond a physical achievement.

options.text: Because it is also a spiritual, emotional, and personal experience that changes a person forever.
Because it brings national fame and financial rewards.
Because it requires help from international climbers.
Because it is a test of political dominance.

subject: english
text: What was the cricket's excuse for not saving food for the winter in the poem 'The Ant and the Cricket'?
explanation: The cricket was lazy and spent the pleasant seasons singing, oblivious to the fact that winter was approaching.

options.text: He spent all his time singing and enjoying the warm, sunny summer and spring.
He could not find any food in the entire region.
The ants had stolen all his food reserves.
He was too sick to search for food.

subject: english
text: What was the ant's famous policy when the cricket came asking for food and shelter?
explanation: The ant tells the cricket that while they are his servants and friends, ants follow a strict principle of neither borrowing nor lending.

options.text: We ants never borrow; we ants never lend.
Work hard in winter, sing in summer.
Help the needy, but punish the lazy.
Share your food with all your neighbors.

subject: english
text: When did the Giant realize that he had been selfish in Oscar Wilde's story 'The Selfish Giant'?
explanation: The Giant's heart melted when he saw children playing in the garden and realized that the Spring had avoided his garden because of his selfishness.

options.text: When he saw that the Spring came back only to the parts of the garden where children were playing.
When his wall was knocked down by a strong storm.
When the Hail and the North Wind started destroying his castle.
When he grew too old to walk in his garden.

subject: english
text: What did the Giant do to make the children feel welcome in his garden?
explanation: The Giant took a great axe and knocked down the wall he had built, allowing the garden to become a playground for the children.

options.text: He knocked down the wall with an axe and played with them.
He built a play school for them inside his castle.
He gave them gold coins and fruits from his trees.
He invited their parents to a feast.

subject: english
text: What did the Giant find under the tree in the corner of his garden many years later when he was old?
explanation: The Giant saw his favorite child under the tree; the child had wounds on his hands and feet, showing he was Christ, who invited the Giant to his garden (Paradise).

options.text: The little boy standing under a tree covered with white blossoms and golden fruit, with prints of nails on his hands and feet.
A hidden treasure chest left by the children.
A group of fairies dancing around a magical peach tree.
The little boy had passed away due to the cold winter.

subject: english
text: In 'The Treasure Within', what kind of drawings did Hafeez Contractor make when he was not interested in class lectures?
explanation: Hafeez Contractor used to design fortresses, weaponry, and structural layouts when he was distracted in class, showing his early talent for architecture.

options.text: Sketches of forts, guns, and ammunition
Portraits of his teachers and classmates
Landscapes of hills and rivers
Drawings of flowers and animals

subject: english
text: According to Hafeez Contractor, how does he now design a house for a client?
explanation: Hafeez states that he assesses his client's lifestyle and personality to create a customized design that matches their taste.

options.text: He looks at the client's face, clothes, speech, and taste to understand their personality.
He relies on standard computer software templates.
He asks them to fill out a long questionnaire.
He designs whatever he likes without consulting the client.

subject: english
text: In the story 'Jalebis', what argument did the coins in the boy's pocket use to tempt him to buy jalebis?
explanation: The coins argued that fresh, hot jalebis are meant to be consumed, and since he had money, he should buy them immediately.

options.text: Jalebis are meant to be eaten, and only those with money in their pocket can eat them.
The fees could be paid next month without any fine.
His parents would be happy if he brought sweet jalebis home.
The jalebis were free for students who got good marks.

subject: english
text: How did the school master, Ghulam Mohammed, punish boys who failed to pay their fees on time in 'Jalebis'?
explanation: The boy feared the cane of Master Ghulam Mohammed, who used to make students stand on the bench until the last bell.

options.text: He made them stand on the bench for hours.
He sent them home and suspended them.
He called their parents to the school.
He gave them extra homework.

subject: english
text: Choose the correct option to fill in the blank: 'She behaves as if she _______ the owner of the house.'
explanation: The past subjunctive 'were' is used after 'as if' to indicate an imaginary or hypothetical condition, regardless of the singular subject.

options.text: were
is
was
has been

subject: english
text: What is the antonym of the word 'Obsolete'?
explanation: 'Obsolete' means no longer produced or used (out of date), and 'modern' is its direct antonym.

options.text: Modern
Ancient
Broken
Hidden

subject: english
text: Choose the option that correctly changes this sentence into indirect speech: The doctor said to him, 'Take these medicines regularly.'
explanation: The reporting verb 'said to' is changed to 'advised' for medical instructions, and the demonstrative pronoun 'these' becomes 'those'.

options.text: The doctor advised him to take those medicines regularly.
The doctor told him to take these medicines regularly.
The doctor ordered him that take those medicines regularly.
The doctor advised him to take these medicines regularly.

subject: english
text: Which of the following sentences has the correct word order with the adverb 'scarcely'?
explanation: The adverb 'scarcely' at the beginning of a sentence requires inversion of the subject and auxiliary verb ('had I arrived') and is paired with 'when'.

options.text: Scarcely had I arrived at the station when the train left.
Scarcely I had arrived at the station than the train left.
Scarcely had I arrived at the station than the train left.
Scarcely I arrived at the station when the train left.

subject: english
text: Complete the sentence with the correct preposition: 'He is blind _______ his son's faults.'
explanation: The phrase 'blind to' is an idiom meaning unwilling or unable to perceive or acknowledge something (like faults). 'Blind in' is used for physical sight.

options.text: to
of
with
at

subject: english
text: Identify the sentence that is grammatically correct regarding the use of the comparative degree.
explanation: When comparing one thing with others of its class using comparative degree, 'any other' must be used to exclude the subject from the rest.

options.text: Gold is more precious than any other metal.
Gold is more precious than any metal.
Gold is most precious than any other metal.
Gold is precious than any other metal.

subject: english
text: What is the meaning of the phrasal verb 'put up with'?
explanation: 'Put up with' means to tolerate or bear with a difficult situation or person without complaining.

options.text: To tolerate or endure
To postpone a meeting
To build a structure
To stay at a hotel

subject: english
text: Which of the following sentences contains a correct inversion for emphasis?
explanation: When a negative adverb like 'seldom' starts a sentence, the auxiliary verb ('have') must precede the subject ('I'), followed by the past participle ('seen').

options.text: Seldom have I seen such a beautiful painting.
Seldom I have seen such a beautiful painting.
Seldom did I saw such a beautiful painting.
Seldom have I saw such a beautiful painting.

subject: english
text: Identify the grammatical error in this sentence: 'The reason why he failed is because he did not study.'
explanation: Using 'the reason why... is because' is redundant. The correct structure is 'the reason why... is that'.

options.text: 'because' should be replaced with 'that'
'why' should be replaced with 'which'
'did not' should be replaced with 'had not'
There is no error in this sentence.

subject: english
text: Choose the sentence that is free from error regarding modifier placement:
explanation: The introductory phrase 'To write a good essay' must modify the subject of the main clause. In option B, the subject is 'you', which is correct.

options.text: To write a good essay, you must first formulate a clear thesis statement.
To write a good essay, a clear thesis statement is required.
A clear thesis statement is required to write a good essay.
Writing a good essay, a clear thesis statement must be formulated by the student.

subject: english
text: Identify the sentence that correctly uses a participle to combine these sentences: 'The sun set. We returned home.'
explanation: Since the two clauses have different subjects ('the sun' and 'we'), a nominative absolute construction ('The sun having set') is used.

options.text: The sun having set, we returned home.
Setting the sun, we returned home.
The sun set, we returned home.
The sun having setting, we returned home.

subject: english
text: Which of the following sentences shows the correct use of 'prefer'?
explanation: The verb 'prefer' is followed by the preposition 'to', not 'than' or 'over'.

options.text: He prefers tea to coffee.
He prefers tea than coffee.
He prefers tea more than coffee.
He prefers tea over coffee.

subject: english
text: Identify the correct classification of the underlined word: 'This is the very book I was looking for.'
explanation: In this context, 'very' is used as an emphasizing adjective modifying the noun 'book' (meaning 'actual' or 'precise').

options.text: Adjective
Adverb
Conjunction
Pronoun

subject: english
text: Choose the correct idiom to fill in the blank: 'He decided to _______ and admit his mistake to the teacher.'
explanation: 'To make a clean breast of it' means to confess or admit to something fully and honestly.

options.text: make a clean breast of it
beat around the bush
burn his boats
cry over spilled milk
